description: Bounded clean-room edge-insertion profile for minimizing the maximum lifted-triangle slope on convex triangles and non-coplanar lifted quadrilaterals.

source.title: Optimal Triangulation
source.author: Tiow-Seng Tan
source.algorithm_paper: M. Bern, H. Edelsbrunner, D. Eppstein, S. Mitchell, and T. S. Tan, Edge Insertion for Optimal Triangulations, Discrete & Computational Geometry 10(1), 47-65 (1993), DOI 10.1007/BF02573962
source.copyright: The chapter and paper are copyrighted publications; this package independently implements a bounded algorithmic profile and includes no copied source code.

input.vertex_order: strict convex boundary order in the xy projection, clockwise or counterclockwise; no three projected vertices collinear
input.lifted_general_position: For N=4, reject four coplanar lifted points. N=3 is always permitted after projected convexity validation.

output.meaning: 1-based rank of the optimal maximum slope among distinct slopes of all 3-vertex subsets; slope ties collapse to one rank

algorithm_details.objective: For a triangle, solve z=f(x,y); its slope is sqrt((df/dx)^2+(df/dy)^2). The triangulation objective is the largest triangle slope, minimized over triangulations. Implementations compare squared slopes exactly as rational numbers by cross multiplication.
algorithm_details.exact_arithmetic_bounds: With coordinates in [-8,8], each projected determinant has absolute value at most 512, each gradient numerator at most 512 in absolute value, squared-slope numerator at most 524288, denominator at most 262144, and cross-products at most 137438953472; signed 64-bit arithmetic is sufficient.
algorithm_details.primary: Begin with the 0-2 fan. Inspect triangles attaining the current maximum in listed order, and their vertex IDs in increasing order. A vertex q is an anchor when its nonzero steepest-descent ray (-gradient) lies in the closed projected tangent wedge of that triangle; a boundary ray counts. For the unique remaining vertex s, insert q-s only if it properly crosses the triangle's opposite edge. Replace the two fan triangles and accept only a strict reduction in maximum squared slope. At most one flip exists for N=4.
algorithm_details.independent_oracle: Enumerate the sole triangulation at N=3 or both quadrilateral triangulations at N=4, compute each maximum slope directly, and choose the smaller objective.
algorithm_details.tie_and_degeneracy: Strictly convex projected order and no three projected points collinear are required. Four lifted points must not be coplanar, matching the edge-insertion paper's general-position assumption; degenerate lifted quads are rejected instead of applying its simulated perturbation. Equal slope values compare equal, all tied worst triangles are considered, and an equal-objective flip is not taken.
algorithm_details.primary_complexity: Constant work for at most two triangles and four vertices, plus exact ranking of at most four triple slopes.
algorithm_details.oracle_complexity: At most two triangulations, each containing two triangles, plus exact ranking of at most four triple slopes.
